solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Idiot happy with parking in force

indicators.note: in places the happy-plus-parking letters within the word for the force

parts.note: the Met is London's Metropolitan Police force
feeling up means feeling cheerful
P is the standard road-sign abbreviation for parking

explanation.surface: A cheerful fool parked inside a police station.
explanation.definitionFit: Muppet is British slang for a foolish or incompetent person, from the puppet show.

clue.text: Wind, average a shade up

parts.note: the mean is the arithmetic average

indicators.note: in a down clue, up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: red is a shade or colour

explanation.surface: Describes something being a little above average in tone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'up' turns RED into DER beneath MEAN.
explanation.definitionFit: To wind, as a river does, is to take a twisting, meandering course.

clue.text: Rare element in London theatre

definitions.meaning: a rare metallic element of the platinum group, symbol Pd
a famous variety theatre in London's West End

explanation.surface: Something rare found inside a London playhouse.
explanation.definitionFit: The same word names both the scarce platinum-group metal and the celebrated West End venue.

clue.text: Time to parade last of maggots in apple

indicators.note: in puts that single letter inside the apple word

parts.note: an eater is a dessert apple, one for eating raw rather than cooking

indicators.note: last of picks out only the final letter of the word maggots

explanation.surface: A maggot wriggles out of an apple, as if ready to march.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition plays on the Easter parade, a festive procession in bonnets.
explanation.definitionFit: The spring festival is a traditional occasion for a bonneted procession, the Easter parade.

clue.text: Underground network not giving dog a brush then?

parts.note: the pet that is not a dog here is the other household favourite, a cat
a comb is used, like a brush, for grooming hair

explanation.surface: A puzzled question about grooming a pet, tacked onto tunnels.
explanation.walkthrough: Read cryptically: not giving the dog a brush, but giving the cat a comb.
explanation.definitionFit: Catacombs are subterranean burial galleries forming a network of tunnels.

clue.text: Ascendant king letting in a little light?

indicators.note: rising, in a down clue, means the word is read upwards

parts.note: a raja is an Indian king or prince

explanation.surface: A rising monarch lets in a glimmer, like a dawning sun.
explanation.definitionFit: A door left slightly open lets a sliver of light through the gap.

clue.text: Sanctimonious nob briefly subordinate to a workers' supervisor?

indicators.note: in a down clue, subordinate to means placed underneath the a

parts.note: pi is slang for piously self-righteous

indicators.note: briefly cuts the last letter off the word for a nob

parts.note: an aristo, an aristocrat, is a nob or toff

explanation.surface: A smug toff is demoted to work under a factory boss.
explanation.walkthrough: The workers are worker bees, hence the question mark.
explanation.definitionFit: A beekeeper looks after hives of worker bees, a whimsical sort of supervisor.

clue.text: Stuffed with paper, one forced in many cases

indicators.note: stuffed with means the paper's letters are packed inside
forced suggests the letters of one being pushed out of shape

parts.note: FT is the Financial Times, the paper this crossword appears in

explanation.surface: Someone is force-fed newspaper in numerous instances.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forced' is the anagram signal, rearranging the word one; 'Stuffed with' looks like describing someone but marks the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that happens frequently occurs in many cases.

clue.text: Grand in deposit, adequate capital

indicators.note: in places the grand's letter inside the deposit word

parts.note: to bank money is to deposit it
G is short for a grand, a thousand pounds or dollars
OK means satisfactory, adequate

explanation.surface: A thousand put on deposit is a decent amount of capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'capital' looks like money but is a capital city.
explanation.definitionFit: Thailand's chief city is the seat of its government.

clue.text: Titan ending in court, finally

parts.note: Atlas is the Titan of Greek myth who holds up the sky

indicators.note: ending in picks the final letter of court

explanation.surface: A mighty figure's case concludes in court at long last.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase expresses relief that something has come about in the end.

clue.text: A poet on the far side of loch in Scottish town

indicators.note: in an across clue, on means placed after
the far side of a word is its last letter

parts.note: John Milton, author of Paradise Lost

explanation.surface: A bard stands across the water from a Scottish lake.
explanation.definitionFit: A town in South Lanarkshire, near Glasgow.

clue.text: Bob, perhaps, has to show contrition at first, entering small dwelling

indicators.note: entering puts the show-plus-letter inside the small dwelling

parts.note: a hut is a small, simple dwelling
to air is to show or display

indicators.note: at first takes the opening letter of contrition

explanation.surface: Bob apologises on stepping into a cottage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name; it is the short hairstyle, and 'perhaps' marks it as one example.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is one style of cut-and-trim at the hairdresser's.

clue.text: Amazed, I fancy, to inhale soft drug

indicators.note: to inhale means to take in, so the soft letter goes inside
fancy as an adjective means elaborate, signalling the letters being rearranged

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for soft

explanation.surface: Someone astonished imagines breathing in a mild narcotic.
explanation.definitionFit: Valium is a brand of this tranquilliser, a sedative medication.

clue.text: He scored with honest talking

indicators.note: talking signals that the word for honest is heard, not seen

parts.note: frank means honest and outspoken

explanation.surface: Someone succeeded by speaking candidly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'scored' looks sporting, but means wrote music: César Franck was a Belgian-French composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Composers score their works, and César Franck wrote music such as his Symphony in D minor.

clue.text: Marry — discard income?

parts.note: read as discard in come: bin, to discard, put inside come

explanation.surface: A wedding prompts someone to give up their earnings.
explanation.walkthrough: Split 'income' into 'in come' and it says put a word for discard (BIN) in COME.
explanation.definitionFit: To marry two things is to join or unite them.

clue.text: Perch for bird

definitions.meaning: a bar or rod a bird can sit on
a wading marsh bird such as the water ...

explanation.surface: A roost for a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both a horizontal bar to rest on and a family of marsh birds.

clue.text: Which carrier did you say requires space to fix on first of baggage?

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of baggage

parts.note: room means space
to stick is to fix or fasten on

explanation.surface: A traveller asks an airline which carrier has room for luggage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Which ... did you say' sounds 'witch': the definition is a witch's carrier, the broomstick she flies on.
explanation.definitionFit: A witch traditionally travels by flying on a besom, so it is her means of transport.

clue.text: Present doctrine designed to impress university

indicators.note: to impress means to press into, so the university letter is set inside
designed means arranged anew, signalling an anagram

explanation.surface: A doctrine is crafted to win over a university.
explanation.definitionFit: To present someone is to make them known to another, a synonym for making acquainted.

clue.text: Come together when vote cast in Irish parliament

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters within the parliament

parts.note: the Dáil is the lower house of the Irish parliament

indicators.note: cast suggests throwing the letters into a new shape

explanation.surface: Members unite when a ballot is held in the Dáil.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like voting but shuffles VOTE to OVET.
explanation.definitionFit: Plans that fit neatly together interlock like a wood joint of that name.

clue.text: Mother and son, perhaps, not entirely great — that's nonsense

parts.note: mum is an informal word for mother

indicators.note: not entirely drops the last letter

parts.note: a son is an example of a boy
jumbo means very large, great

explanation.surface: Family relations described as less than great, dismissed as rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means meaningless ritual or gibberish talk.

clue.text: Very big day before relaxing rest

indicators.note: before means the day comes ahead of the other piece

parts.note: Mon is short for Monday

indicators.note: relaxing suggests loosening the letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A huge day precedes a lazy rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Monster can be an adjective for something huge or gigantic.

clue.text: Second, then first — go no further!

parts.note: top means first, the best

explanation.surface: A runner placed second and then first is told to halt.
explanation.definitionFit: The command to halt tells someone to proceed no further.

clue.text: Colourful flower in taupe, surprisingly

indicators.note: surprisingly signals the letters coming out in an unexpected order

explanation.surface: A bright bloom turns up in a drab brownish-grey.
explanation.definitionFit: A garden bedding plant with vivid trumpet-shaped blooms.

clue.text: Soak, assuming cold stew

indicators.note: assuming means taking on, so the soak word takes in the cold letter

parts.note: to souse is to soak or drench
C is the abbreviation for cold on taps

explanation.surface: A drunk takes a chilly bowl of stew.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Soak' could be a drunk, but it is the verb. Scouse is a Liverpool meat stew, which gave Liverpudlians their nickname.
explanation.definitionFit: Scouse is a meat-and-potato hotpot from Liverpool.

clue.text: Money thief

definitions.meaning: British slang for a pound sterling
someone who nicks, that is steals, things

explanation.surface: Cash and a crook.
explanation.definitionFit: British slang uses the word for a pound coin and also for someone who steals.

clue.text: South American animal, fur on one

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above

parts.note: an animal's fur is its coat
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A South American creature's pelt worn on someone.
explanation.definitionFit: A raccoon-like mammal with a long ringed tail from Central and South America.

clue.text: Result of last punch, a beauty!

definitions.meaning: a boxing finish where the final blow fells the opponent
slang for a stunningly attractive person

explanation.surface: A boxer's final blow lands, and it's a stunner.
explanation.definitionFit: The word is both a decisive boxing win by a blow and slang for someone gorgeous.

clue.text: Somewhat cynical, a senator, unfortunately

indicators.note: Somewhat says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A rather jaded politician, sadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Alas is an interjection of regret, used like sadly or regrettably.

clue.text: Possible call to get a grip on endless party woes

indicators.note: getting a grip on means holding, so the call wraps round the party

parts.note: tails is one call when a coin is tossed

indicators.note: endless drops the final letter

parts.note: a rave is a dance party

explanation.surface: A coin-toss call is held to blame for a party's troubles.
explanation.definitionFit: Travails are painful hardships or troubles.

clue.text: The fall of Richard Nixon?

parts.note: fall is the American word for the season after summer, so the President's fall is that season

explanation.surface: The downfall of a disgraced US president.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue looks like Watergate, but an American such as Nixon calls the season after summer 'the fall'.
explanation.definitionFit: Americans call the season of falling leaves the fall; Britons use another name.

clue.text: Dry, Sun god out more then?

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
the opposite of out is in
the opposite of more is less

explanation.surface: Arid, the sun god being away more often.
explanation.walkthrough: 'then?' says take the opposites: out becomes IN and more becomes LESS.
explanation.definitionFit: Weather with no precipitation is dry.

clue.text: Wilder state, conventional city?

parts.note: Gene Wilder was an American comic actor
VA is the postal abbreviation for Virginia

explanation.surface: An actor's state judged to be a run-of-the-mill city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'conventional' means home of the Geneva Conventions on the conduct of war.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swiss city gave its name to the international treaties on humanitarian law.
